content.introduction: The sources indicate that Schwab provides a six- to 12-month outlook for stock sectors through its Schwab Sector Views, which are set by the Schwab Center for Financial Research. These views are based on a factor-based approach combined with market and economic assessments and are positioned across a five-point spectrum: Least Favored, Less Favored, Neutral, More Favored, and Most Favored. The outlook is intended to help investors make tactical shifts in their portfolios and is updated monthly. The specific ratings for October 2026 are not provided in the sources.
body:
Our outlook on the 11 S&P 500 equity sectors.

October 2, 2026•Schwab Center for Financial Research

   
   
   
   

Image 1

  

_Schwab Sector Views is our six- to 12-month outlook for stock sectors, which represent broad sectors of the economy. The Schwab Center for Financial Research (SCFR) combines a factor-based approach with a market and economic assessment to determine the ratings. For the basics on sectors, please see__Stock Sectors: What Are They? How Are They Used?_ [...] Investors who want to make tactical shifts in their portfolios can use Schwab Sector Views ratings as a resource. These ratings can be helpful in evaluating and monitoring the domestic equity portion of a portfolio. These favorability views are our preferences for investment assets relative to their peers shown in each section. The views reflect a six- to 12-month outlook and may change as markets evolve. Views do not guarantee future returns and are not a forecast that an asset will rise or [...] The views are positioned across a five-point spectrum: Least Favored, Less Favored, Neutral, More Favored, and Most Favored. The Schwab Center for Financial Research (SCFR) sets these views. The team employs a robust, data-driven approach to guide investors managing cross-asset positions in a globally diversified portfolio. The investment approach incorporates a wide range of quantitative data and qualitative inputs that assess the current market environment relative to historical context.
